findings.impact: The style gate fails on this character alone.

findings.original: not just a reporting tool, but a transformation engine
findings.impact: Sounds like a slogan and tells the CFO nothing concrete.

options.label: Say what it does
options.text: a reporting platform that [NEED: the concrete capability]
options.mightLose: The rhetorical lift of the contrast.

findings.original: It will eliminate reporting errors and reduce recruiting costs by 40% within 30 days.
findings.defect: Unconditional guarantee with no baseline, method, source, or approval.
findings.impact: It is the main financial reason given for approval, and nobody has authorized it.

options.label: Remove the guarantee
options.mightLose: The proposal's only stated financial benefit, until an approved estimate exists.

options.label: Replace with an approved estimate
options.text: We estimate [NEED: approved savings range] lower recruiting costs, measured against [NEED: baseline] from go-live.
options.consequence: Keeps a benefit the CFO can check.

findings.original: Industry experts agree this is the future of recruiting.
findings.impact: The CFO cannot know who agrees or why, and it weakens trust in the rest.

options.label: Cite a named source
options.text: [NEED: named, approved source and what it found].
options.consequence: Keeps the point if a source exists.

findings.impact: The CFO cannot tell which amount is being approved.

options.label: State a discount
options.consequence: Keeps $100,000 if a discount was approved.
options.mightLose: Simplicity: adds a term to confirm.

findings.original: The rollout takes six weeks. Work begins September 15, 2026, and will be complete by October 1, 2026.
findings.defect: September 15 to October 1 is 16 days, not six weeks.
findings.impact: The CFO cannot plan resources or payment timing.

options.label: Keep the duration, drop the dates
options.text: The rollout takes six weeks from [NEED: start date after approval].

options.label: Keep the dates, fix the duration
options.text: The rollout takes about two weeks, from September 15 to October 1, 2026.
options.consequence: Consistent, but only if two weeks is feasible.
options.mightLose: The buffer a six-week plan implied.

findings.original: The migration is reversible, although the only legacy database and its backups will be permanently deleted during launch.
findings.defect: Contradiction: reversible, yet the only data and backups are deleted.
findings.impact: The CFO would approve permanent data loss believing it can be undone.

options.label: Say it is permanent
options.text: The migration cannot be reversed: the only legacy database and its backups will be permanently deleted during launch.
options.mightLose: The reassurance that the migration is reversible.

options.label: Keep a rollback window
options.text: The migration is reversible until [NEED: retention end date], when the legacy database and its backups are deleted.
options.mightLose: A simple plan; needs retention confirmed first.

findings.original: Customer questions will receive a response soon.
findings.defect: Implies a support service level nobody approved.
findings.impact: The CFO may assume support terms are covered by the price.

options.label: Point to agreed terms
options.text: Support terms, including response times, are [NEED: agreed support terms].

findings.original: Delivery Lead also owns final scope-change approval.
findings.defect: Two owners of the same final approval.
findings.impact: Scope changes drive cost, and it is unclear who controls them.

options.label: One final approver
options.text: Delivery Lead contributes to scope changes; Account Lead gives final approval.
options.mightLose: Delivery Lead's authority to block a change.

findings.original: Both roles support transition to support.
findings.defect: No one owns the transition to support.
findings.impact: The handoff can fall between the two roles.

options.label: Name the owner
options.text: Delivery Lead owns transition to support; Account Lead contributes.
options.mightLose: Shared responsibility, if that was intended.

findings.impact: They dilute credibility in a purchase decision.

findings.original: In conclusion, this groundbreaking partnership will unlock meaningful value across your evolving talent landscape.
findings.defect: Empty closing with no decision or owner.
findings.impact: Ends on filler instead of the ask.

options.label: End with the ask
options.text: Please approve the purchase by [NEED: decision date] so work can start after approval.
options.consequence: Gives the CFO a concrete next step.
